hard-prohibition.application: Name the exact action that must not happen, explain the consequence, and give the permitted alternative. Keep exceptions explicit so a narrow safety rule does not become a ban on unrelated work.

worked-examples.application: Choose a decision that prose alone leaves ambiguous. Show the unwanted case and the intended case close together, then explain the distinction the examples are meant to teach.

generated-file-guard.application: Identify the generated file or region, its editable source, and the command that rebuilds it. State whether the generated diff belongs in the change and which nearby files remain hand-maintained.

verification-matrix.application: Map each kind of change to the checks it needs. Include setup requirements and explain what the default command skips, so a passing narrow check is not mistaken for complete coverage.

nested-instructions.application: Keep shared rules at the root and place subsystem guidance beside the code it describes. Explain how to find the applicable files and how to resolve conflicting instructions.

single-source.application: Link to the file that owns a changing fact instead of copying its value into instructions. Give enough context to locate and interpret that authority without creating another list to maintain.

skill-routing.application: Map recognizable tasks to specific guides and say when to read them. Keep the entry file useful as an index, with detailed workflows in the documents that own them.

behavioral-conditioning.application: Turn a recurring mistake into a concrete decision rule: what to establish before editing, how far to expand scope, or when a question should stay read-only. Connect the rule to an observable action.

house-vocabulary.application: Define terms that are easy to confuse and specify where the convention applies. Preserve literal identifiers and quoted source when a prose convention would otherwise change their meaning.

architecture-narrative.application: Follow a request or piece of data through the system, naming the components and boundaries it crosses. Explain ownership and the reason for a boundary so readers can apply it to a new case.

ratchet.application: Name the baseline or compatibility boundary and the direction in which it may change. Pair the rule with an enforcement command, and explain any gaps that still require review.

contribution-etiquette.application: Describe the project’s expectations for public actions, review updates, and commit or PR text. Explain workflow costs and permission boundaries before an agent opens, posts, or pushes something.

scope-layering.application: State how to determine which role or contribution context applies before listing its permissions. Include a fallback for cases where identity or access cannot be verified.

context-budget.application: Give injected material an owner and a size limit. Describe when it is loaded, how it affects existing context, and which changes need extra review for cost or prompt stability.
